acceptance: The worker attests quiescence when leaked futures finish, or an evidence-gated operator release exists; documented in the proof matrix
Jobs store and expose a shared outcome (failed/incomplete/completed) derived from the result
Staging cleanup waits for quiescence or purge
Outstanding-work detection reads the result object, with a test using the real export shape
context: 2026-10-04 concurrency adversarial review. MCP claim/fence/publish transactions were checked and found sound; these are outcome and capacity gaps around them.
description:
Findings in benchbox/mcp/jobs.py (develop 8ed0c64e1):
1. Capacity leak (confirmed): when a job has outstanding throughput work, jobs.py:1174-1182 calls mark_unknown_outstanding and skips quiescence attestation. Nothing later calls attest_quiescence for that job (only :1152 and :1222). Each throughput timeout permanently uses up a running slot: with defaults (max_running_per_principal=2, max_running=8), two timeouts lock out a tenant and eight stop the server. No operator release path exists. The proof matrix covers only a dead worker.
2. Outcome (confirmed by code): jobs.py:1183 checks only top-level response["status"] == "failed". The success path (mcp/tools/benchmark.py:516-526) never sets it, and mcp_metadata.status="no_results" is ignored. Runs with failed queries, contained throughput or a None result publish as completed. _public_status (:1374) does not expose the ADR's shared outcome.
3. Staging (plausible): lease recovery (jobs.py:1141-1146) deletes staging {execution_id}-{attempts}, the directory a fenced old attempt may still write to, contrary to ADR section 4. A recreated directory is never purged.
4. Detection (plausible): if both result exports fail (mcp/tools/benchmark.py:318-324), the response is {} plus metadata, so _response_has_outstanding_work finds nothing and the job publishes as completed while threads run. The proof test uses a synthetic {"outstanding_stream_ids"} shape, not the real phases.*.outstanding_work export.
